entries.name: Trout and char daily quota
entries.regs_verbatim: Zone B Daily Quotas. Trout/char: 5, but not more than 1 over 50 cm, 2 from streams, 2 lake trout, 1 bull trout. NOTE: Bull trout may only be retained from Oct 16-Aug 14. These fish may only be from the Liard River watershed (or other specified waters) and only 30-50 cm in length. And you must release: Rainbow trout of any size from streams, May 1-June 15, Lake trout under 30 cm, Lake trout of any size, Sept 15-Oct 31, Bull trout from the Liard River watershed Aug 15-Oct 15, and from the Peace River watershed all year.

rules.review_reason: The PEACE half of a sentence naming two watersheds with different windows. The verbatim keeps the whole sentence so the reader can see what it is a half OF; the extent and the absent window are what make this rule the Peace one. The Liard half has no zone rule (WINDOWS_HELD_ELSEWHERE): the Liard River Watershed row prints the same release (liard_river_watershed.r1, Aug 15-Oct 15) and r10 releases bull trout across Zone B all year.

rules.verbatim: These fish may only be from the Liard River watershed (or other specified waters) and only 30-50 cm in length.
rules.review_reason: THE NOTE'S IMPLICATION, as the user settled it (2026-09-24): bull trout may be kept only from the Liard River watershed or other specified waters, so across Zone B they are catch and release. The Liard row (r7:liard_river_watershed…@7-53) and every row printing its own bull trout limit speak over it at the water's rank.

entries.name: Peace River navigation
entries.regs_verbatim: PEACE RIVER The Peace River is no longer navigable past the Site C construction site. Avoid boat travel between 2 km upstream of the dam site (warning signs are on shore) and the downstream construction bridge. See https://www.sitecproject.com/boating for details.

rules.verbatim: PEACE RIVER The Peace River is no longer navigable past the Site C construction site. Avoid boat travel between 2 km upstream of the dam site (warning signs are on shore) and the downstream construction bridge.
rules.review_reason: Shown on the Peace River as a note, never colouring it: the reach it names (2 km upstream of the Site C dam site to the downstream construction bridge) has no cut-point at either end — only `peace_river__site_c_dam` exists.

entries.name: Thin ice — Inga and Sundance
entries.regs_verbatim: THIN ICE AND OPEN WATER Due to aeration projects, dangerous thin ice and open water may exist on Inga and Sundance lakes. It is prohibited to enter within the fenced area surrounding the aerator.

rules.verbatim: Due to aeration projects, dangerous thin ice and open water may exist on Inga and Sundance lakes.
It is prohibited to enter within the fenced area surrounding the aerator.
rules.extent_text: the fenced area surrounding the aerator
rules.review_reason: A PROHIBITION ON ENTERING a fenced area, not an angling closure — typed hazard until an access type can say 'do not enter' without implying a fishing ban. Placed on the two lakes (Sundance is `wbk:329473810`, the polygon r7:sundance_lake@7-32 matched); the fenced area itself has no polygon.

entries.name: Ice fishing huts
entries.scope_note: SPLIT: one sentence carried a 'should' and an offence. Rendering both as law is the mirror of rendering law as advice.

entries.name: Site C telemetry
entries.regs_verbatim: NOTICE TO ANGLERS BC Hydro is tracking the movement of fish throughout the Site C Reservoir, Peace River and its tributaries using acoustic and radio telemetry to gather valuable data on the potential effects of the Site C project on fish. Anglers who catch tagged fish are encouraged to return them to the water if possible, or return the tag by e-mailing tagreturns@golder.com or calling (250) 785-9281. If tags come from anywhere other than the Site C Reservoir, Peace River and its tributaries, please call the regional Ministry office in Fort St. John at (250) 787-3415.
